verdict.reasoning: Patient reports a few days of sore, red, very itchy skin interfering with sleep and work focus: "it's been a few days now. I have like a sore and a red skin... it's itching a lot, like all the time. And I can't even sleep at night... when I'm in the meeting... I can't actually think about what I have to say." Doctor later summarizes "last four days"; 3–4 days is a reasonable approximation.
Duration and characteristics: "it's been a few days now. I have like a sore and a red skin. It's... really itchy" and doctor: "you mentioned it all started three days ago. Four days ago."
Patient: "And I can't even sleep at night."
Patient: "even at work... it's really annoying because I can't actually think about what I have to say. I'm always like, disturbed by this disease."

Distribution: patient: "Mostly like my chest, my. My hands, my arms" and later clarifies: "No, just the chest, hands, and, like, inside the elbows." No face: "On my face. No." Legs not involved: when doctor says "arms and legs as well?" patient replies "No, just the chest, hands, and, like, inside the elbows."

Dry/cracked, no bleeding or discharge: patient: "my skin is a bit cracked in some parts" and to question about pus/blood: "No." Doctor: "You haven't seen any other pus or blood coming out of your skin?" Patient: "No."

No triggers or changes: doctor asks about triggers including shower gel, clothing, contacts; patient: "No. It's actually, like... I'm thinking about maybe I should change something because I haven't and I don't understand." This supports no identified triggers, no new soaps/clothes.

Hiking worsened symptoms: patient: "I like first instance hiking during the weekend and I... I can't really do it anymore because it's like very like... I wanted to do that last weekend and it was super painful."
No fever: doctor asks about "temperature or fevers?" Patient: "No. Just the itching."
No cough or SOB: doctor: "your chest is okay. No cough? No. Breathing difficulties?" Patient: "No."
Bowel/urinary function okay: doctor: "so your bowels are working okay... You're passing urine Okay?" Patient: "I think so."
Past treatment helped: patient re prior eczema treatment: "they gave me like some cream and something... At that time? Yes [it helped]."
OTC steroid last night no relief: patient: "I bought like a steroid cream at the pharmacy last night, but it apparently didn't help because it's still itching a lot today."
OTC antihistamines tried without relief: patient: "I have tried antihistamines lately, but it didn't really help."
History of eczema: patient: "earlier I was like prescribed for my eczema" and later: "I had eczema before."
Remote asthma: patient: "No, I just had asthma in the past. But not anymore?"
No regular meds: doctor: "do you take any regular medications at the moment?" Patient: "No."
Same as hpi-012: "I bought like a steroid cream at the pharmacy last night, but it apparently didn't help."
Same as hpi-013: "I have tried the antihistamines... But it didn't really help."
No allergies: doctor: "Do you have any allergies at all?" Patient: "Oh, allergies. No."
Age: patient: "So I live with a few flatmates. So, you know, I'm 31."
Living situation: patient: "So I live with a few flatmates... I'm living with a few people to save money."
Job: patient: "I work at a pharmaceutical company... I'm a. Like a kind of project manager."
Non-smoker: doctor: "do you smoke at all?" Patient: "No."
Alcohol: patient: "once in a while... a few. A few beers per week. Something like this."
Doctor impression: "I do wonder whether this is a flare up of your eczema. The reason being that you said it's quite itchy..." This is pruritic dermatitis likely eczema flare.

Doctor summary: "for the last four days, you've had very itchy skin, very sore skin... mainly your chest" and later confirms "just the chest, hands, and, like, inside the elbows" plus "you've got some dry skin and some cracked skin as well" and patient denied "pus or blood." Erythematous is inferred from "red skin."
Afebrile is supported by negative fever history: doctor asks about "temperature or fevers?" Patient: "No. Just the itching."

Assessment includes prior eczema and OTC treatment response: history of eczema discussed; limited response to steroid cream and antihistamines: "it apparently didn't help" and "it didn't really help."
Impairing sleep and function: patient: "I can't even sleep at night" and describes difficulty focusing at work and stopping hiking due to pain/itch.

Doctor: "I wonder whether giving you stronger prescription of a steroid may be beneficial, which I'm happy to prescribe to you today... use... over the next week to 10 days." This aligns with a stronger topical corticosteroid for 7–10 days.
Doctor: "I'm going to give you something, some emollients which helps to moisturize the skin to use in the bath and shower. And it's definitely worth using that for the first seven to 10 days."

Doctor: "I can give you something a little bit stronger today as well. Something like fexofenadine, which I can give to you today. It's definitely worth trying it." This is a trial of prescription fexofenadine due to poor response to OTC antihistamines.

Doctor: "it's also worth keeping a diary of any triggers which are affecting your symptoms. Anything you wear or anything you use in terms of shower gels or soap. Because if that's causing your symptoms, then we need to have a discussion about that next time I see you."

Doctor: "do come back and see me next week if things don't get better." This implies follow-up in about a week if not improving; earlier return for concerns is standard inference though not explicitly phrased.
